reason: The cited evidence (all from the same paper) confirms that oxygen contamination up to ~1 wt.% occurs in powder-metallurgy HfNbTaTiZr and causes embrittlement and phase instability, and that powder metallurgy yields finer microstructures. However, none of the cited passages mention electrical conductivity, carrier scattering, or in situ structural–electrical correlation; the key mechanistic and predictive premises are therefore unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Oxygen contamination in powder-metallurgy HfNbTaTiZr can reach ~1 wt.% and causes embrittlement and prevents single-phase solid solution formation
Powder metallurgy processing yields finer grain sizes and different microstructures (e.g., porosity, precipitates) than arc melting
Spark plasma sintering of gas-atomized powder can produce dense, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr with low oxygen content
Oxygen-induced defects (precipitates, lattice distortions, grain boundaries) act as scattering centers that reduce carrier mobility
In situ structural characterization can quantitatively correlate microstructural features with electrical conductivity
